Project: React. Upgrade being assessed: 17 -> 18.
This change was introduced in release 18. Source: How to Upgrade to React 18 (official_migration_guide). Section: Updates to Client Rendering APIs.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
For more information, see the working group discussion here. If your app doesn't work after upgrading, check whether it's wrapped in <StrictMode>. Strict Mode has gotten stricter in React 18, and not all your components may be resilient to the new checks it adds in development mode. If removing Strict Mode fixes your app, you can remove it during the upgrade, and then add it back (either at the top or for a part of the tree) after you fix the issues that it's pointing out.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Updates to Client Rendering APIs: When you first install React 18, you will see a warning in the console: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18. Use createRoot instead. Until you switch to the new API, your app will behave as if it's running React 17. Learn more: https://reactjs.org/link/switch-to-createroot React 18 introduces a new root API which provides better ergonomics for managing roots. The new root API also enables the new concurrent renderer, which allows you to opt-into concurrent features. // Before import { render } from 'react-dom'; const container = document.getElementById('app'); render(<App tab="home" />, container); // After import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'; const container = document.getElementById('app'); const root = createRoot(container); // createRoot(container!) if you use TypeScript root.render(<App tab="home" />); We've also changed unmountComponentAtNode to root.unmount: // Before unmountComponentAtNode(container); // After root.unmount(); We've also removed the callback from render, since it usually does not have the expected result when using Suspense: // Before const container = document.getElementById('app'); render(<App tab="home" />, container, () => { console.log('rendered'); }); // After function AppWithCallbackAfterRender() { useEffect(() => { console.log('rendered'); }); return <App tab="home" /> } const container = document.getElementById('app'); const root = createRoot(container); root.render(<AppWithCallbackAfterRender />); There is no one-to-one replacement for the old render callback API — it depends on your use case. See the working group post for Replacing render with createRoot for more information. Finally, if your app uses server-side rendering with hydration, upgrade hydrate to hydrateRoot: // Before import { hydrate } from 'react-dom'; const container = document.getElementById('app'); hydrate(<App tab="home" />, container); // After import { hydrateRoot } from 'react-dom/client'; const container = document.getElementById('app'); const root = hydrateRoot(container, <App tab="home" />); // Unlike with createRoot, you don't need a separate root.render() call here. For more information, see the working group discussion here. If your app doesn't work after upgrading, check whether it's wrapped in <StrictMode>. Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 18 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 18 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18. Until the app switches to the new root API, it behaves as if it is running React 17.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 18, where ReactDOM.render is no longer supported.
quotes: When you first install React 18, you will see a warning in the console: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18.
conditions.relevance: Ties the removal of ReactDOM.render to React 18.

conditions.statement: The application calls ReactDOM.render to mount its root.
quotes: Until you switch to the new API, your app will behave as if it's running React 17.
conditions.relevance: The text names ReactDOM.render as the API affected by the change.

suggested_actions: Replace render(<App />, container) with const root = createRoot(container); root.render(<App />); importing createRoot from 'react-dom/client'.

paths.description: unmountComponentAtNode has been changed to root.unmount in React 18.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 18, where unmountComponentAtNode is changed to root.unmount.
quotes: React 18 introduces a new root API which provides better ergonomics for managing roots.
conditions.relevance: Ties the root API change to React 18.

conditions.statement: The application calls unmountComponentAtNode to unmount a root.
quotes: We've also changed unmountComponentAtNode to root.unmount:
conditions.relevance: The text names unmountComponentAtNode as the API changed to root.unmount.

suggested_actions: Replace unmountComponentAtNode(container) with root.unmount() on the root created by createRoot.

paths.description: The callback argument to render has been removed in React 18 because it usually does not have the expected result when using Suspense.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 18, where the callback argument to render is removed.
quotes: React 18 introduces a new root API which provides better ergonomics for managing roots.
conditions.relevance: Ties the render callback removal to the React 18 root API change.
ambiguities: The text does not state that the callback removal itself is tied to release 18 by a version label; it is in the same section as the React 18 root API change.

conditions.statement: The application passes a callback as the third argument to render.
quotes: We've also removed the callback from render, since it usually does not have the expected result when using Suspense:
conditions.relevance: The text names the render callback as the removed feature.
ambiguities: The text states there is no one-to-one replacement, so the migration depends on the use case.

suggested_actions: Move the callback logic into a component that calls useEffect, and render that component with root.render.
Check the working group post for Replacing render with createRoot for use-case-specific guidance.

paths.description: Apps using server-side rendering with hydration must upgrade hydrate to hydrateRoot.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 18, where hydrate is replaced by hydrateRoot.
quotes: React 18 introduces a new root API which provides better ergonomics for managing roots.
conditions.relevance: Ties the hydrate change to the React 18 root API.

conditions.statement: The application uses server-side rendering with hydration and calls hydrate.
quotes: if your app uses server-side rendering with hydration, upgrade hydrate to hydrateRoot:
conditions.relevance: The text names hydrate as the API to upgrade for SSR with hydration.

suggested_actions: Replace hydrate(<App />, container) with const root = hydrateRoot(container, <App />); importing hydrateRoot from 'react-dom/client'.
Do not call root.render() after hydrateRoot, since it is not needed there.

paths.description: Strict Mode has gotten stricter in React 18 and adds new checks in development mode that not all components may be resilient to, which can make the app stop working after upgrading.

conditions.statement: Upgrade crosses release 18, where Strict Mode is stricter.
quotes: Strict Mode has gotten stricter in React 18, and not all your components may be resilient to the new checks it adds in development mode.
conditions.relevance: Ties the stricter Strict Mode to React 18.

conditions.statement: The application wraps its tree in StrictMode.
conditions.relevance: The text names StrictMode as the component to check.

suggested_actions: If the app breaks, remove StrictMode during the upgrade.
After fixing the issues Strict Mode points out, add StrictMode back at the top of the tree or for a part of the tree.
